messages:
SalesAmy: quick heads-up — Acme POC load test (internal) started hitting 503s ~2m after ramp to ~200 rps. Customer reporting timeouts and some 5xx spikes. Can oncall / infra triage?
EngOncall_Jon: on it. Do we have request IDs or a log bundle?
Customer_CT: sending one sample, saw it at 12:03:45 UTC — request_id:req_x7b9. Response payload: \u003c503 overload\u003e. It happens across multiple endpoints not just /chat.
SalesAmy: attaching a snippet from their run (they'll DM full logs):
```
2026-03-20T12:03:45Z ERROR svc inference - status=503 err="overloaded" req=req_x7b9 backend=worker-7 latency_ms=812
2026-03-20T12:03:46Z WARN  queue dispatcher - queue_size=120 inflight=48
```
SRE_Lina: looks like queue backlog + worker lag. Autoscaler may be slow to react for sudden fanout. Can we confirm current pool sizes and backlog metrics?
InfraBot: current state: worker-pool replicas=3, burstpool-enabled=true, burstpool-active=1, queued-requests=118, avg-kv-cache-hit=0.12. Recent events: scale_trigger_at 12:02:10 -> pending scale-up.
EngOncall_Jon: autoscaler emitted scale plan but provisioning lagged ~45s. If backend takes 30-40s to register, that explains the window of 503s.
Solutions_Raj: customer is asking about pricing for burstpool spikes and max sustained throughput. Can we give a ballpark for extra hours if we push temporary capacity?
SalesAmy: Raj — they want to know before we start any manual scale ops.
SRE_Lina: technical first — mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase worker-pool to 6 replicas (fastest), 2) enable pre-warm of burstpool to 3 instances, 3) reduce max_concurrency/per-worker to lower queuing pressure (trade latency). Also enable fallback routing to smaller model if requests queue > 80.
EngOncall_Jon: I'll run a manual scale now and add a short-lived canary routing change to prefer dedicated nodes. Command: 
```sh
kubectl -n inference scale deployment worker-pool --replicas=6
# then toggle routing: redwoodctl route update --prefer dedicated --threshold-queue=80
```
InfraBot: action queued: scale job submitted by EngOncall_Jon at 12:04:12 UTC.
EngOncall_Jon: scaled to 6, respawn observed, worker join logs look healthy. Monitoring backlog.
InfraBot: update: replicas=6, burstpool-active=2, queued-requests=26, avg-latency=220ms.
Customer_CT: seeing immediate improvement, 503s reduced, but still occasional spikes during a 30s ramp window. Thanks.
SRE_Lina: follow-ups: we should tune the autoscaler cooldown to be more aggressive for POC environments (reduce stabilization window), and add a short-lived pre-warm rule for scheduled load tests. I'll open a runbook PR.
Solutions_Raj: pricing note: short burstpool hours are billed at hourly rate + pro-rata. For this specific 20m manual bump, we can absorb minor overage under the POC support package — I'll confirm with finance and message the customer.
SalesAmy: I'm telling Acme we'll cover this 30m bump and will follow up with a brief post-mortem and recommended config for their long running tests.
EngOncall_Jon: root cause summary for ticket: rapid fanout -> queue build -> autoscaler provisioning lag -> transient 503s. Short-term mitigation applied (manual scale + prefer-dedicated). Long-term: adjust scale cooldowns, implement scheduled pre-warm, add a small edge-circuit that fails over to smaller model for high-queue events.
SRE_Lina: adding link to monitoring graph: https://monitoring.internal/redwood/acme-poc/queues?t=last_30m
Customer_CT: thanks everyone — will re-run their 5k request test tomorrow with your recommended config.
SalesAmy: fine. I'll loop in finance + engineering for a quick playbook we can reuse on future POCs. :thumbsup:
EngOncall_Jon: nudge to docs team: add a short checklist for sales-led POCs: expected burst billing, scheduled pre-warm step, recommended load ramps.
SRE_Lina: created PR with runbook checklist and autoscaler tuning suggestions.
SalesAmy: great—closing this thread once we confirm next test. :white_check_mark:
